title: kate-core: read editorconfig from one handle
summary: read_editorconfig opens the file before it checks the size. It re-checks metadata on that handle. It then reads at most one byte past the cap. A larger read is skipped and not parsed. This packet does not edit workspace.rs. Linux CI runs the tests.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust. It does not need a window or a review by the owner. Linux CI runs the tests. Also run cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin.

definitions.definition:
fn read_capped(file: &mut std::fs::File) -> std::io::Result<Option<String>>

pub fn read_editorconfig(start: &std::path::Path) -> ModeOverride

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Open the path with File::open. Read metadata from that handle, not from a second path lookup. If the handle is not a file or its length is over MAX_EDITORCONFIG_BYTES, return without reading. Otherwise read with take(MAX_EDITORCONFIG_BYTES + 1). If the string is longer than the cap, skip it and do not parse it. A skipped file does not set root. Keep the directory test and the oversized test. Do not edit workspace.rs. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: modeline::tests::read_capped_stops_past_the_cap
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because read_capped does not exist. A handle whose bytes exceed the cap returns Ok(None). A small root = true file returns that text.
